scenes.text: This frog freezes solid every winter, and comes back to life in spring.
It's the wood frog, and up to sixty percent of its body turns to ice.
Its heart stops beating, and it stops breathing completely.
In Alaska, wood frogs can stay frozen like this for up to seven months.
The trick is sugar: its body floods its cells with glucose, which works like antifreeze.
When spring comes, it thaws out and hops away like nothing happened.
Would you want to hibernate like a frog popsicle?

title: This frog freezes solid and comes back to life 🐸
caption: Wood frogs let up to 60% of their bodies freeze in winter. Their heart and breathing stop, and glucose acts as antifreeze so they can thaw out in spring. 🐸
